title: Expanding the Development Horizon
subtitle: Ensuring Welfare, Inclusion, and Empowerment for Rural and Tribal Communities
body_text:
India’s development story is reaching deeper into rural and tribal communities, transforming access, opportunity, and quality of life. From basic services and resilient infrastructure to livelihoods, skills, education, and financial security, interventions are expanding the foundations of inclusive growth. Focused efforts for women, tribal communities, and vulnerable groups are further strengthening pathways to dignity and empowerment. These initiatives are reshaping rural India through wider opportunity, stronger communities, and more equitable development.
From Welfare Delivery to Decentralised Partnerships
Direct fiscal transfers to gram panchayats have been increased. It has been increased from ₹2.36 lakh crore under the 15 th Finance Commission (2021–26) to ₹4.35 lakh crore under the 16 th Finance Commission (2026–31). The Union Budget for rural development has been increased from ₹87,765 crore (2016–17) to ₹2.73 lakh crore (2026–27). The Union Budget for tribal affairs has been increased from ₹4,826 crore (2016–17) to ₹15,421.97 crore (2026–27).
Foundations of Dignity: Universal Access to Basic Needs
Jal Jeevan Mission
Household tap water coverage increased from 3.23 crore (August 2019) to over 15.91 crore (August 12, 2026). As of August 12, 2026, 2.89 lakh villages have reported 100% tap water coverage under Har Ghar Jal campaign.
Swachh Bharat Abhiyan - Grameen
Over 12.19 crore individual household toilets have been constructed, as of August 12, 2026. India was declared Open Defecation Free in 2019 . Over 1,288 GOBARdhan biogas plants are operational, as of August 11, 2026, compared to 14 plants in FY 2018-19.
Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana
As of August 12, 2026, over 10.57 crore free LPG connections have been provided to women from below-poverty-line households . The total number of LPG connections in India has increased from 14.52 crore in 2014 to 33.39 crore in 2026.
Universal Village Electrification
100% willing household electrification (pan-India level) was achieved by March 2019 under PM Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana (SAUBHAGYA) . Under the Deendayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana , 100% village electrification was achieved by 2025 .
Ayushman Bharat
More than 45.51 crore Ayushman Cards have been issued as of August 12, 2026. 96.43 crore ABHA accounts have been created as of August 12, 2026. Over 1.86 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs are currently functional (as of August 12, 2026).
Food Security for All
PM Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana provides free foodgrains to over 81.35 crore beneficiaries. 99.8% Fair Price Shops under the PDS are automated for Aadhaar-based distribution , as of July 29, 2026. Ration cards are 100% digitised across all States/UTs as of July 29, 2026. As of July 29, 2026, over 221 crore portability transactions have been recorded under One Nation One Ration Card .
Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan (Sarva Shiksha Abhiyaan)
Between 2018-19 to 2025-26, 4,073 schools have been upgraded and 1.49 lakh ICT and digital initiatives implemented. Further, 25,000 schools are covered under skill education . 97.3% of the schools are equipped with functional female sanitation facilities. F emale drop-out rate at primary school level decreased from 4.6% (2013-14) to 0.1% (2025-26). At secondary school level , it reduced from 14.5% (2013-14) to 8% (2025-26).
Reservation for Economically Weaker Section and Improved Enrolment Levels
10% EWS reservation provided for candidates outside existing SC, ST, and OBC reservation categories in 2019. This decision benefits the economically disadvantaged individuals from the general category. In 2025-26, Gross Enrollment Ratio (GER) was recorded 89.4 at primary level and 81.5 at secondary level. GER at higher secondary level increased to 61.7 in 2025-26 as compared to 46.4 in 2014-15.
Beti Bachao Beti Padhao
Girls’ Gross Enrollment Ratio (GER) for girls at the secondary level (Classes 9–10) rose from 75.5% in 2014–15 to 83.4% in 2025–26 .
Kasturba Balika Vidyalayas and PM eVidya
The number of sanctioned schools increased from 3,609 (2014–15) to 5,639 (2024-25). Operational KGBVs stand at 5,133, as of 2024–25. Enrolment increased from 3.52 lakh (2014–15) to 7.11 lakh (2024).
The SWAYAM portal (India’s indigenous MOOC platform) has over 6.5 crore enrolments (as of August 12, 2026). As of August 12, 2026, DIKSHA has 2.35 crore registered users.
Building the Backbone: Infrastructure and Connectivity
Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana – Grameen
Under PMAY-G, over 3.91 crore houses have been sanctioned, and 3.13 crore houses have been completed (as of August 12, 2026).
Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana
As of June 2026, 99.6% of eligible habitations have been connected with all-weather roads . Completed length of roads increased from 3.86 lakh km (May 2000 – May 2014) to 4.13 lakh km (May 2014 – August 12, 2026). Completed number of bridges rose from 484 to 10,404 during May 2014 – August 12, 2026.
Digitalization of Gram Panchayats
Under BharatNet , 2.19 lakh Gram Panchayats (GPs) are connected as of May 2026. Through eGramSwaraj , over ₹3 lakh crore in payments have been processed, as of June 2026. O ver 1.28 lakh GPs are using SabhaSaar for creating meeting summaries, as of June 2026.
Pathways to Prosperity: Livelihoods, Skills, and Financial Security
Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM)
As of August 12, 2026, 10.19 crore households have been mobilised into 94.46 lakh SHGs.
As of July 29, 2026, 3.46 crore Lakhpati Didis have been created.
Role of Community Resource Persons in Ensuring Last-Mile Delivery of Schemes
Over 9 lakh CRPs are currently active, serving thematic areas like agriculture, banking, insurance and nutrition. This includes more than 50,548 Bank Sakhis , 1.91 lakh Krishi Sakhis, 2,012 Matsya Sakhis, and 1.70 lakh Pashu Sakhis .
Introduction of Self-Help Entrepreneur Mart (SHE-Mart)
Announced in the Union Budget 2026-27, aiming to benefit 1 crore women . Aims to create community-owned retail spaces for women under the SHG ecosystem.
Deendayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana
Candidates trained increased from 43,038 in 2014–15 to 18.45 lakh till August 11, 2026. Candidates placed rose from 21,446 in 2014–15 to 12.35 lakh till August 11, 2026.
Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana
Over 1.64 crore youth have received skill training since inception till June 2026.
Viksit Bharat - Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin)
Total persondays generated between FY 2006-07 to FY 2013-14 were 1,660 crore, whereas, between FY 2014-15 to FY 2024-25, it rose to 3,029 crore. Women’s participation increased from 48% (FY 2013–14) to 58.19% (FY 2024–25).
e-Shram Portal
Registrations increased from 14.40 crore (Dec 2021) to 31.87 crore (August 12, 2026).
PM Vishwakarma Yojana
As of August 12, 2026, over 30 lakh traditional artisans have been registered . As of August 12, 2026, 24.32 lakh artisans have received skill training and 17.70 lakh have received toolkits.
PM SVANidhi
Number of beneficiaries has increased from 26.37 lakh (Nov 2021) to 78.17 lakh (August 12, 2026). As of August 12, 2026, loans amounting to ₹ 18,971.18 crore have been disbursed . 46% of the beneficiaries are women.
PM MUDRA Yojana
Total number of loans sanctioned have increased from 3.49 crore (2016) to over 59.14 crore (July 2026).
PM Jan Dhan Yojana
Number of beneficiaries have increased from 17.9 crore (Aug 2015) to 58.90 crore (August 12, 2026).
Expanding Social Security Coverage
Under National Pension System , beneficiaries increased from 1.05 crore (2016–17) to 2.17 crore (2025–26). Under Atal Pension Yojana , beneficiaries increased from 48.80 lakh (2016–17) to 9.29 crore (June 2026). 27.90 crore people covered by Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana up to July 2026. 58.78 crore people covered under Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana up to July 1, 2026. More than 54 lakh unorganised sector workers have been registered under Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-dhan scheme as of July 2026.
Accelerating Tribal Development through Integrated Interventions
Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN)
As of August 5, 2026, 540 Van Dhan Vikas Kendras (VDVK) have been sanctioned, benefiting 46,042 persons from Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups .
Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Vikas Mission (PM-JVM)
4,172 Van Dhan Vikas Kendras sanctioned, benefitting 12.48 lakh tribals under this scheme, as of August 2026.
Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Unnat Gram Abhiyan (PM-JUGA)
It combines the efforts of 17 ministries and focuses on filling long-standing gaps in tribal-majority villages and PVTG habitations. Under PM JUGA, the emphasis has increasingly moved from isolated interventions to coordinated, mission-mode delivery across sectors and ministries. In last 12 years-
7.60 lakh tribal houses have been completed and 28,303 tribal villages have access to drinking water . 59,812 tribal households and public institutions have been electrified and 657 Anganwadi Centres have been operationalized in tribal areas. 692 hostels have also sanctioned for tribal students.
Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY)
As of August 12, 2026, over 4.16 lakh Scheduled Caste (SC) houses have been built, over 4.17 lakh SC households are covered under health protection schemes , and more than 3.57 lakh SC households have individual toilets. 17,578 villages have been declared Adarsh Grams as of August 12, 2026.
Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRSs)
Operational schools increased from 129 (2014–15) to 511 (August 12, 2026). As of August 12, 2026, EMRSs have an enrolment of 1.68 lakh students.
PM-YASASVI
20.61 lakh students have received pre-matric scholarship, and 24.53 lakh students have received post-matric scholarship for FY 2024-25.
Scholarships for Scheduled Tribe (ST) Students
Between April 2024 and August 12, 2026, Pre-Matric Scholarship Scheme has benefitted more than 28.99 lakh tribal students. National Fellowship for ST Students supported 2,961 research scholars in 2025–26. 56% of the beneficiaries were females.
Scholarships for Higher Education for Young Achievers Scheme (SHREYAS)
The Top-Class Education for SC Students scheme enabled 8,571 students to study in leading institutions such as IITs, IIMs, NITs and AIIMS in 2025-26.
National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE)
89,915 sewer and septic tank workers and more than 2.81 lakh waste pickers have been validated as of July 2026.
Scheme for Economic Empowerment of De-Notified Tribes (SEED)
During 2025-26, ₹26.75 crore was disbursed for the educational empowerment of 4,485 De-Notified Tribe (DNT) students . 73,569 Ayushman Bharat cards have been issued to DNT families, under the health component, during 2025-26.

enrichment.summary: A PIB backgrounder dated 13 August 2026 consolidates cumulative achievements across rural and tribal development schemes in India, covering fiscal devolution, basic services, infrastructure, livelihoods, financial inclusion, social security and targeted tribal/SC interventions. It highlights that Gram Panchayat fiscal transfers rose from ₹2.36 lakh crore under the 15th Finance Commission to ₹4.35 lakh crore under the 16th Finance Commission, and that flagship programmes such as Jal Jeevan Mission, Swachh Bharat-Grameen, PMAY-G, PMGSY, DAY-NRLM and PM-JANMAN have expanded coverage substantially since 2014-15. The document also details growth in financial inclusion (Jan Dhan, MUDRA, PM SVANidhi), social security (NPS, Atal Pension Yojana, PMJJBY/PMSBY) and tribal/SC welfare schemes (PM-JVM, PM-JUGA, PM-AJAY, EMRS, PM-YASASVI).
enrichment.context:
This backgrounder is a consolidated 'report card' style release typical of government communication ahead of milestone anniversaries (here, positioned toward 2026-27, close to 80 years of independence and mid-way through the Amrit Kaal vision of Viksit Bharat@2047). It stitches together progress under multiple centrally sponsored and central sector schemes launched or scaled up since 2014, reflecting the government's emphasis on last-mile delivery, saturation-based coverage (e.g., Har Ghar Jal, 100% village electrification, 100% digitised ration cards) and convergence of ministries (PM-JUGA integrates 17 ministries for tribal development). The increased Finance Commission devolution to Gram Panchayats reflects the constitutional mandate under Article 280 and the 73rd Amendment for strengthening fiscal federalism and local self-government, a recurring UPSC theme on Panchayati Raj institutions and cooperative/competitive federalism.

The release also reflects the evolution of India's welfare architecture from scheme-based delivery to platform-based, technology-enabled governance — leveraging the JAM trinity (Jan Dhan-Aadhaar-Mobile), DBT, e-Shram, eGramSwaraj and BharatNet for digital last-mile delivery. Tribal development components (PM-JANMAN for Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups, PM-JVM for Van Dhan Vikas Kendras, PM-JUGA for saturation of tribal villages) build on the historical Tribal Sub-Plan strategy and PESA Act's emphasis on targeted, community-based empowerment. Similarly, women-centric interventions like SHG-based Lakhpati Didi and the newly announced SHE-Mart under Budget 2026-27 build on the DAY-NRLM's decade-long community mobilisation model. Such consolidated releases are useful for aspirants to track scheme evolution, budgetary trends, and quantifiable outcome indicators frequently tested in Prelims and used as substantiating data in Mains answers on inclusive growth, social justice and governance.

prelims_questions.question: As per a 2026 PIB backgrounder on rural development, direct fiscal transfers to Gram Panchayats increased to ₹4.35 lakh crore under the award period of which Finance Commission?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states that Gram Panchayat transfers rose from ₹2.36 lakh crore under the 15th Finance Commission (2021-26) to ₹4.35 lakh crore under the 16th Finance Commission (2026-31).

prelims_questions.question: The Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN), mentioned in the release for sanctioning Van Dhan Vikas Kendras, is specifically targeted at which group?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release notes that PM-JANMAN's Van Dhan Vikas Kendras benefit persons from Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs), a sub-category of Scheduled Tribes identified as most marginalised.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of enhanced fiscal devolution to Panchayati Raj Institutions under successive Finance Commissions for strengthening grassroots democracy and inclusive rural development in India.

Examine how convergence-based, mission-mode interventions such as the Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Unnat Gram Abhiyan (PM-JUGA) mark a shift in India's approach to tribal development, and assess the challenges in achieving saturation-level coverage in tribal-majority villages.
